newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Baan tops ADR trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Baan tops ADR trade.

text.p: Shares in Dutch software company Baan Co NV rose in heavy trade on Wednesday buoyed by a strong earnings report and a recommendation for the stock.

Most European shares and American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were firmer because of a weakening dollar and rising New York markets, said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
Baan was up 1-7/8 to 43-1/2 with almost 1.5 million shares traded at midday, nearly three times its normal volume. The stock was the most active among foreign shares and ADRs.

The increase came after the company reported sharply higher revenues, earnings and earnings per share for 1996's fourth quarter. UBS Securities analyst Joseph Farley upgraded his rating for the shares to buy from hold and Smith Barney raised Baan's target price and earnings estimates.
Britain's LucasVarity Plc fell 1-3/8 to 33-3/4 after the Financial Times newspaper's Lex column said it was hard to see the company's shares outperforming.

Latin American shares were largely flat as investors remained uneasy about volatility in world markets. Brazilian bellwether Telebras fell 5/8 to 85-1/8 despite a congressional first step toward allowing re-election of reformist President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Japan's Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd rose 2-1/4 to 44-7/8 as investors returned to the stock, thinking it had been oversold, a trader said.
Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd rose one to 55-1/8 in light trade after the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration approved two new drugs.
Decliners led advancers 261 to 219 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 41 million shares in early afternoon.
